# Surface reference

Contents:
- [Generated by the script](#generated-by-the-script) — tile, widget, shortcuts, share, processtext
- [Add by hand](#add-by-hand) — notification listener, live wallpaper, accessibility service, direct share, deep links
- [Not extensible](#not-extensible) — things users often assume are pluggable but are not

---

## Generated by the script

### Quick Settings tile (`tile`)

API 24+. A `TileService` bound by the system only while the shade is open.

```xml
<service
    android:name=".DemoTileService"
    android:exported="true"
    android:icon="@drawable/ic_surface"
    android:label="@string/app_name"
    android:permission="android.permission.BIND_QUICK_SETTINGS_TILE">
    <intent-filter>
        <action android:name="android.service.quicksettings.action.QS_TILE" />
    </intent-filter>
</service>
```

Things that catch people out:

- `qsTile` is null outside the listening window. Always null-check before
  calling `updateTile()`, or the tile crashes on rotation and odd lifecycles.
- The icon is tinted by the system. Use a flat single-colour vector; anything
  with detail or multiple colours turns into a silhouette.
- `subtitle` requires API 29+ and is **not** a silent no-op below that — calling
  it on API 26–28 throws `NoSuchMethodError` and the tile dies. Guard it with an
  `SDK_INT` check, as the generated service does. This is the sort of failure
  that never appears in CI and only shows up on an older device.
- On Android 13+, `StatusBarManager.requestAddTileService()` prompts the user
  to add the tile directly. This is by far the best onboarding — without it the
  user has to find the tile in the edit screen and drag it up.
- A tile that needs to launch UI should use `startActivityAndCollapse()`, which
  on Android 14+ takes a `PendingIntent` rather than an `Intent`.

### Home screen widget (`widget`)

An `AppWidgetProvider` (a `BroadcastReceiver`) plus an `appwidget-provider` XML
descriptor. Layouts are `RemoteViews`, which supports only a restricted view
set: `LinearLayout`, `FrameLayout`, `RelativeLayout`, `GridLayout`, `TextView`,
`ImageView`, `Button`, `ProgressBar`, `ListView`, and a few others. Custom views
throw at inflation time.

- `updatePeriodMillis` is clamped to a 30-minute minimum, and the system may
  ignore it entirely. For anything more responsive, drive updates from
  WorkManager or a broadcast rather than expecting the descriptor to deliver.
- Android 12+ applies rounded corners and dynamic colour automatically. Set
  `targetCellWidth`/`targetCellHeight` (API 31+) so the widget sizes sensibly on
  a Pixel's grid; `minWidth`/`minHeight` remain the fallback for older versions.
- `PendingIntent` must specify `FLAG_IMMUTABLE` or `FLAG_MUTABLE` on API 31+.
  Omitting both throws.
- Jetpack Glance is the modern way to build these with Compose, but it adds a
  dependency tree. Not worth it for a prototype.

### App shortcuts (`shortcuts`)

Static shortcuts declared in `res/xml/shortcuts.xml`, referenced by a
`<meta-data android:name="android.app.shortcuts">` on the launcher activity.
Limit is five per app, and the launcher usually shows four. Dynamic shortcuts
via `ShortcutManager` can be added and reordered at runtime.

The `<intent>` element requires an action; without one the shortcut silently
fails to appear.

### Share sheet target (`share`)

An `<intent-filter>` for `ACTION_SEND` with a MIME type. `ACTION_SEND_MULTIPLE`
handles multiple items. The app appears in the sheet's app row.

Position in the sheet is decided by the system based on usage — it cannot be
forced. To appear in the top "direct share" row, publish sharing shortcuts (see
below).

### Text selection action (`processtext`)

`ACTION_PROCESS_TEXT` with `text/plain`. Appears in the selection popup's
overflow menu system-wide, which makes it one of the most useful and least-known
surfaces.

Return `EXTRA_PROCESS_TEXT` in the result to replace the selection — only works
when the field is editable. Read `EXTRA_PROCESS_TEXT_READONLY` to know which
case applies. Use `Theme.NoDisplay` or `Theme.Translucent.NoTitleBar` so the
activity does not flash a window.

## Add by hand

### Notification listener

```xml
<service
    android:name=".DemoListenerService"
    android:exported="false"
    android:permission="android.permission.BIND_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_SERVICE">
    <intent-filter>
        <action android:name="android.service.notification.NotificationListenerService" />
    </intent-filter>
</service>
```

Subclass `NotificationListenerService` and override `onNotificationPosted`.

**This reads every notification on the device**, including message content from
other apps. The user must grant it manually in Settings → Notifications →
Device & app notifications; there is no runtime permission dialog. Send them
there with `Settings.ACTION_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_SETTINGS`.

Make sure the user understands the scope of what they are enabling before
suggesting it. Play Store policy also restricts this permission to apps whose
core function requires it.

### Live wallpaper

A `WallpaperService` with an inner `Engine` that draws to a `SurfaceHolder`,
plus `res/xml/wallpaper.xml` and `BIND_WALLPAPER` permission on the service.
Self-contained and harmless, just more drawing code than the other surfaces.

The engine must stop its draw loop in `onVisibilityChanged(false)` or it burns
battery continuously in the background.

### Accessibility service

An `AccessibilityService` can observe and act on UI across the whole system.
It is the broadest grant on Android — effectively full read and control of the
screen. Only appropriate for genuine accessibility tooling. Play Store removes
apps that use it for automation, and the user should be told plainly what it
allows before they enable it.

### Direct share / sharing shortcuts

To appear in the top row of the share sheet, publish dynamic shortcuts with a
matching `<share-target>` in `res/xml/shortcuts.xml` and the
`androidx.sharetarget` dependency. Ranking is still system-controlled. This is
noticeably more work than the plain share target and rarely worth it for a test.

### Deep links / open-with

An `<intent-filter>` with `ACTION_VIEW`, `BROWSABLE`, and a `<data>` scheme
makes the app a handler for matching URLs. Add `android:autoVerify="true"` plus
a hosted `assetlinks.json` to become the default handler without a chooser.

## Not extensible

Users sometimes assume these are pluggable because they look like app slots.
They are not, and it saves time to say so directly:

- **Now Playing** — Pixel-exclusive, no third-party API.
- **At a Glance** — Google-internal; the widget slot is not open.
- **Quick Share** — a fixed system feature, not an extension point.
- **The default assistant** — replaceable wholesale via `VoiceInteractionService`,
  but not extensible in place. App Actions via `shortcuts.xml` capabilities are
  the supported hook, and the surface has been repeatedly reworked.
- **Lock screen** — no general widget support on modern Android.

## Several menu items from one activity

The text-selection popup renders one entry per exported component with a
`PROCESS_TEXT` filter. That does **not** mean one class per action: an
`<activity-alias>` is a manifest-only entry with its own label and filter,
pointing at an activity that already exists.

```xml
<activity-alias
    android:name=".Summarize"
    android:targetActivity=".ProcessTextActivity"
    android:exported="true"
    android:label="@string/task_summarize">
    <intent-filter>
        <action android:name="android.intent.action.PROCESS_TEXT" />
        <category android:name="android.intent.category.DEFAULT" />
        <data android:mimeType="text/plain" />
    </intent-filter>
</activity-alias>
```

The activity reads `componentName.className` to learn which alias was tapped.
Three actions, three manifest entries, zero extra classes.

Two traps:

- The **target** activity must be declared in the manifest too, and can be
  `android:exported="false"` — the alias carries the export.
- Put the aliases in a **flavour** manifest and the menu differs per build,
  which is how `core` shows one action and `nano` shows three. The merger
  combines them; nothing in `src/main` needs to know.

Labels are truncated hard in that popup. Two words is the practical limit.
